data.name: Serbia
data.summary: Serbia (non-EU) taxes residents' worldwide dividends and capital gains at a flat 15%, with capital gains exempt after 10 years of holding and a step-up to market value on arrival for foreign shares. No wealth tax; no inheritance or gift tax for children, and shares/securities are outside inheritance tax altogether. No special regime for wealthy arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if domicile or centre of business and vital interests in Serbia, or 183+ days in a 12-month period. Non-citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains of resident individuals on shares, securities and real estate are taxed at a flat 15%, worldwide, self-assessed. Gains on assets held continuously for at least 10 years are exempt. For shares in non-resident companies acquired before becoming resident, the cost base is the market value on the day the person became resident (step-up on arrival).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Art. 72a: no gain on rights acquired by inheritance in the first order; transfers between spouses and direct-line relatives; assets held continuously 10+ years; government/central bank debt securities. Art. 79: real estate proceeds reinvested in own housing in Serbia within 90 days (refund if within 12 months). Cost is CPI-indexed (art. 74).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Residents (domicile or centre of business and vital interests, or 183 days in any 12-month period) are taxed on worldwide gains with a foreign tax credit (art. 12).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Art. 74(9): for shares in non-resident companies, if the taxpayer was not resident at acquisition and for at least six months after, the acquisition cost is the market value on the day residence began. Capital gains are not included in the annual (10%/15%) additional income tax. Digital assets are taxed separately (15%).

open_questions: How the 10-year holding test applies to portfolios with repeated purchases (FIFO lots) was not checked.
No individual exit tax found; not confirmed against legislation.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat 15% (art. 77) on gains held under 10 years; 0% after 10 years of continuous holding. No local surtax.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Habitual trading could be reclassified as self-employment income; no specific guidance found.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Exempt if held continuously for at least 10 years (art. 72a).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide; foreign tax credit capped at Serbian tax. Step-up to market value on arrival for shares in non-resident companies (art. 74(9)).

dividends.summary: Dividends are capital income taxed at a flat 15% on the gross amount: withheld on Serbian dividends, self-assessed on foreign dividends with a credit for foreign tax up to the Serbian tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Interest on dinar savings and government bonds is exempt.
dividends.important_exceptions: Capital income is not included in the annual additional income tax (10%/15% above three times the average salary).

dividends.rate_basis: Art. 64: 'Stopa poreza na prihode od kapitala iznosi 15%'. No surtax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 20% WHT on dividends paid to non-residents (also 20% to tax havens), reducible by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: About 68 treaties (PwC list), including most EU states, UK, Switzerland, UAE, China, Russia; no treaty with the United States.
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 15%; corporate holding rules not researched.

wealth_tax.summary: Serbia has no net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual local property tax on real estate: for individuals not keeping books, progressive rates capped at 0.40% (base up to RSD 10m) rising to 2.0% for the highest bands; land up to 0.30%; municipalities set rates within the caps (art. 11 Law on Property Taxes).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax applies to real estate, cash, deposits, claims, digital assets, IP and vehicles, but shares and securities are outside its scope. First-order heirs (children, spouse) and the deceased's parents, and first-order donees, pay no tax. Other heirs pay 1.5% (second order) or 2.5% (others).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Art. 21(1)(1) Law on Property Taxes: exempt for the first-order heir, spouse and parent of the deceased, and first-order donees. Art. 14(4): shares and securities excluded; RSD 100,000 per year per category from the same person excluded.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Relationship-based; no residence condition for the exemption.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Since 2022 local governments administer inheritance and gift tax. Inheritance by first-order heirs also gives no capital gain (art. 72a PIT law).

inheritance.gift_tax: Same rules as inheritance: first-order donees exempt; others 1.5%/2.5%. Gifts of shares/securities are outside the tax.
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed: shares are outside the tax and children are exempt.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Taxpayers are residents and non-residents; non-residents for property in Serbia. Scope for foreign assets of residents not material for children (exempt).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if residence or centre of business and vital interests in Serbia, or present 183+ days (continuously or not) in a 12-month period beginning or ending in the tax year; treaty tie-breakers prevail.

routes.name: Temporary residence (single permit)
routes.requirements: Serbia is not in the EU; all foreigners need a temporary residence permit on a recognised ground (work, business, family, property ownership etc.). Grounds and conditions for 2026 not verified.

income.name: Serbia

income_tax.summary: Flat 10% salary tax with a monthly non-taxable amount (about RSD 25,000 per CountryTaxCalc; not applied here), plus employee contributions of 19.9% (self-employed entrepreneurs pay 35.05%) (14% pension, 5.15% health, 0.75% unemployment). A supplementary annual personal income tax of 10% above three times the average annual salary and a further rate above six times applies to high earners (thresholds not given in RSD).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Entrepreneurs (preduzetnici) pay the full contribution themselves at the Article 44(1) rates of the Law on Mandatory Social Insurance Contributions: pension 24% + health 10.3% + unemployment 0.75% = 35.05% of the contribution base (the base is the entrepreneur's own salary, or taxable profit if none, or the lump-sum amount under paušal; Article 22), subject to a minimum and a maximum base (five times the average monthly salary; the RSD amounts were not found, so the cap is left null). Entrepreneurs doing work with enhanced service credit pay a further 3.7-11%. At about EUR 54k (roughly RSD 6.3 million, assuming ~117 RSD/EUR, an assumption) turnover exceeds the RSD 6,000,000 paušal ceiling (Income Tax Law, Art. 40), so the 35.05% on actual profit applies; the paušal option (about RSD 30,000-60,000 a month combined tax and contributions per CountryTaxCalc, an unofficial figure) is not available above that turnover. Income tax on self-employment income is 10% (Art. 38).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Contribution base for employees is between 35.05% and five times the average monthly salary (RSD amounts not found), so the cap is left null. The Income Tax Law page opened shows a monthly non-taxable amount of RSD 37,369 for full-time earnings (indexed yearly; version and 2026 value not confirmed) whereas CountryTaxCalc says about RSD 25,000; neither is applied (effect under ~EUR 400 a year).

regimes.name: Temporary residence for remote workers (reported)
regimes.description: Third-party summaries (WFA) describe a temporary residence permit for people working for foreign employers or clients, with income of at least USD 42,000 a year, health insurance and funds, valid up to one year and renewable. CountryTaxCalc says Serbia has no official digital nomad visa as of mid-2026 and that the temporary-residence permit does not itself grant work authorization. Legal hook: Article 40(4) of the Law on Foreigners lets the Government define categories of foreigners for temporary residence by a separate act, and its example list includes 'stranci digitalni nomadi'; the implementing act and its income test were not found, so the USD 42,000 figure is unconfirmed. No tax change: Serbian tax residency after 183 days (WFA).
regimes.duration_note: Reported as one year, renewable (a 2026 guide not opened says three years).

income.residence_routes: EU, US and many other citizens can enter visa-free for 90 days; longer stays need a temporary residence permit (initially one year, renewable) with a lease, funds, health insurance and criminal record (CountryTaxCalc). Working normally needs entrepreneur registration or a work permit. Permanent residence after five years. Serbia is not in the EU or Schengen.
open_questions: Nomad route: legal basis exists (Law on Foreigners Art. 40(4)) but operating criteria, fees and income test unverified on an official page.
